title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama / Mistral / Qwen (GQA/MQA tuning)
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Model-specific runtime optimizations: updated kernel selection, GQA/MQA quantization thresholds, KV-cache prefetch/eviction heuristics, continuous-batching scheduler improvements. Improves throughput and tail latency for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Some of our largest customers run model families with idiosyncratic execution characteristics (Llama parameter layouts, Mistral attention patterns, and Qwen rotary/kv quirks). This PR adds targeted runtime optimizations to improve throughput and tail latency without changing APIs. It focuses on three areas: 1) kernel selection and small-kernel optimizations for Qwen and Llama, 2) GQA/MQA quantization tuning to reduce memory and improve execution density, and 3) KV-cache and continuous-batching scheduler heuristics tuned for mixed-length workloads.

Summary of changes: consolidated kernel-selection table for model families, added fallback kernels optimized for Qwen rotary patterns, introduced a fast-path for Llama-like ALiBi offsets, implemented GQA/MQA threshold tuning with dynamic scale factors, added KV-cache prefetch + tiered eviction policy, and improved continuous-batching heuristic to group by model-variant and sequence-length percentile rather than raw arrival window.

Performance impact (representative):
- Llama-2-13b: throughput +22% (inference tokens/sec) under continuous batching, P95 latency -18% on 2048-token workloads.
- Mistral-7b: throughput +32% when using tuned MQA profiles, memory working set -1.8x on GQA profile with 8-bit packing.
- Qwen-14b: P95 latency -12% and reduction of soft-faults related to rotary interpolation when using the Qwen-specific kernel fallback.
- Overall cost/unit tokens reduced by ~15% on mixed workloads in our perf-canary.

Testing and validation: unit tests added for kernel selection decision logic and kv cache eviction; integration tests added to runtime-integration and benchmark-lab harness. Perf canary ran across three GPU families (A100, H100, RTX6000) and reported consistent improvements. Added a benchmark dashboard snapshot link in the comment thread.

Compatibility and rollout: changes are behind a runtime feature-flag (runtime.modelOptimizations.v1) and gated by model catalog entries. Default behavior unchanged for customers until rollout is enabled. No public API changes.

Migration notes: operators may want to update Dedicated capacity profiles to enable GQA/MQA enabled kernels on workloads where memory is the bottleneck. Documentation and console toggles added in a follow-up doc PR.

Why this is safe: feature-flagged, covered by unit/integration tests, backed by perf-canary data, and includes automatic fallback to previous kernels when regressions are detected.
